thread:
maria: quick async standup — kernel/batching/KV perf check

maria: what I did: landed the kernel backpressure patch, added a handshake for KV prefetch to avoid double-warmups. ran small perf sweep on canary pool.

maria: blockers: noticed occasional slot-throttle spikes when prefetch and microbatch align; p95 jumps ~2x on one host. need help instrumenting slot handoff paths.

maria: today: add extra tracing, open a tiny canary with handshake enabled for 4 hosts, and queue a follow-up PR for slot metrics.

aj: nice. can you paste the bench snippet? curious about tokens/s after the change. :eyes:

maria: paste from the quick run: 
```
./bench --model=rwd-small --seq=512 --batch=4 --warmups=20
p50: 12.3ms  p95: 38.9ms  tokens/s: 2.8k  (handshake=on)
```

aj: looks promising. can we try the same with handshake=off to compare?

maria: handshake=off run from same host: p50: 11.1ms p95: 81.2ms tokens/s: 2.6k — so p95 improved a lot with handshake but p50 slightly higher. tradeoff seems worth it.

kai: fwiw saw a repro locally where prefetch race + slot handoff leads to a KV cache double-insert and a rare OOM in dev env. stack shows fastpath and slowpath interleaving. I can push a minimal repro.

maria: thanks — can you open a tiny repro issue and tag me? I'll add an explicit compare-and-swap on the prefetch path.

kai: done — https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/987 (repro details + log snippet).

devon: pinging about the PR review: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1234 — I left one comment on the scheduler fairness metric `phi` computation. small nit but affects throttling decisions.

maria: saw it, will address. summary: `phi` tweak reduces slot-steal events in the synthetic burst test. I'll add a unit test for that metric.

sam: ops-bot alerted that one canary host hit 90% GPU mem during the handshake run at 03:14 UTC — trace id `trace-77b`. ops-bot: attach logs?

ops-bot: [auto] attach: /var/log/handshake/trace-77b.log (5 lines) — top line: "prefetch: allocating kv-buffer 128MB" then "evict: triggered by slot-handshake"

sam: probably the double-warmup avoided by handshake still temporarily increases peak mem. we should set a softer mem cap on canary hosts.

maria: agreed — I'll schedule 30m window to run a stress matrix with adjusted mem cap and smaller concurrency, and annotate the canary with mem-cap override.

aj: also throwing this on the backlog: run microbench across seq lengths [128,512,1024] and batch sizes [2,4,8] and capture p50/p95/tokens/s and mem-peak. I can wire up the matrix job.

maria: perfect. aj — can you kickoff the matrix and post results here once done? put `handshake=true/false` variants in the matrix.

aj: will do. ETA ~today EOD.

kai: also quick Q — should prefetch handshake be opt-in via model config or global runtime flag? i feel model-level makes rollouts safer.

maria: model-level is safer for gradual rollout per-customer. but runtime flag helps if we need emergency flip. plan: both — model default + runtime override. will document in the config schema.

devon: thanks. tiny follow-up: when you add tracing, include `slot_id`, `prefetch_token`, and `evict_reason` in the span tags — makes debugging slot collisions easier.

maria: noted. adding those tags.

sam: no blockers from infra, but request: tag canary runs with `handshake-experiment=v1` so billing/metrics pipelines filter them.

maria: will tag.

maria: ok that's it from me. short action list: (1) kai — repro issue (done), (2) maria — add tracing & PR fix, (3) aj — run matrix, (4) devon — confirm `phi` change once tests added, (5) sam — apply mem-cap override for canary.

maria: any objections or other quick asks?

aj: :+1:

kai: thanks, will follow up with repro logs and a small fix suggestion.

devon: :eyes: will pick up tests after lunch.

sam: thumbs on ops changes.

maria: cheers — will post results and link PR when ready.
